decision: Treat the review as a high-rigor cross-language program rather than a screen polish pass
why: The requested scope crosses SQLite migrations Rust DTOs HTTP contracts React state locale chrome viewer controls and responsive presentation; an incorrect persistence shape is expensive to unwind

decision: Chrome is switchable Japanese by default while check content remains the English source text
why: The real demo pack and API expose English requirement content; translating or inventing it would break evidence traceability, while chrome still needs a real locale switch

decision: Attach decisions to immutable runs and represent changed minds as append-only supersession
why: A rerun creates a different run, and a rejection must remain readable after a later acceptance; current currency must be derived from the chain rather than replacing history

decision: Conditional acceptance requires at least one cited finding and a non-empty rationale
why: The condition must bind to evidence the consultant can inspect instead of becoming an unbounded note

decision: Persist decisions in checker SQLite and expose a typed HTTP contract; do not store them in browser state
why: The product promise is recovery months later and the checker already owns immutable runs and SQLite migrations; local state cannot provide an audit trail

decision: Extend the real-process API and browser harnesses before feature completion
why: The repository already has isolated checker and Chromium verification entrypoints; extending them produces rerunnable evidence instead of relying on screenshots or compile success

decision: Completion requires a persisted decision flow plus P0 locale truth and every listed P1/P2 design correction verified on the real service and browser
why: The critique is about drift between documented domain rules and shipped routes, so a component-only patch would leave the product failure intact

decision: Web production build passes and serial typecheck passes
why: The first parallel typecheck raced the build while .next types were being generated; the serial rerun removed that observation-method failure

decision: Checker Rust tests are blocked by a missing Rust toolchain in this environment
why: `cargo`, `rustc` and `rustup` are not installed, so service verification cannot run here until the toolchain prerequisite exists

decision: Scope is eight verifiable units across one SQLite migration two decision endpoints one typed API mirror one review state machine four UI trees five priority hardening areas and one meeting mode
why: The critique names 66 bilingual slash strings 36 sub-12px sites six unnamed viewer controls and a missing terminal decision; the work is cross-cutting but can be separated at the HTTP contract and UI domain boundaries

decision: Rust service verification is the first environment blocker; browser verification is available after the web build
why: No cargo rustc or rustup executable exists in the current environment; npm typecheck and production build both pass serially, so frontend-only work can proceed but backend claims cannot be closed here

decision: Use a decision row with id runId outcome rationale citedFindingIds createdAt supersedesDecisionId and supersededBy plus a current-row unique index
why: Decision facts stay immutable while a transactional chain pointer makes one current decision per run unambiguous; citations are validated against the same run and conditional acceptance cannot be empty

decision: Rust toolchain restored in the user-local cargo path and checker baseline passes
why: The initial blocker was an environment path/toolchain issue rather than a repository failure; all 30 checker tests now pass with the explicit toolchain path

decision: Implemented and verified append-only run decisions with conditional evidence and supersession
why: The real checker scenario proves validation, persisted evidence, one-current enforcement, history retention and restart readability; the forward pointer is intentionally not an FK because the transaction updates predecessor metadata before inserting its successor

decision: Added the terminal decision composer and persisted locale switcher
why: The reviewer can select accept reject or conditional accept, cite findings, enter rationale, save an evidence JSON record and switch Japanese or English chrome while retaining English source findings

decision: Replaced false all-pass and no-incomplete claims with measured ladder and outcome states; removed implicit provenance fallback; added finalization confirmation
why: A zero-band run now says only that no findings are present while OutcomeBar carries the evaluated and not-applicable facts; incomplete sections render only when the API reports them; real Chromium proves the dialog and server lock

decision: Enforced product tokens, 44px touch floor and locale-only chrome in lint plus the Button size scale
why: The critique's 12px floor, raw-colour and bilingual-slash findings were text rules; check-design-rules.mjs now rejects them mechanically and the Button scale carries h-11 on mobile with sm: desktop heights
result: VERIFIED by lint and browser measurement

decision: One delivery page mounts exactly one combined viewer; the workspace's separate combined-view section was merged into the findings-review section
why: The workspace mounted CombinedDeliveryViewer twice (its own section plus ReviewScreen's), so each revision was fetched twice, two IFC workers ran, and window.__modelshelfViewer pointed at only one controller

decision: Deleted FindingInspector and moved its section cut, property inspection and reset-view controls into the review EvidencePanel
why: Merging the sections left FindingInspector with no consumer while the review panel already owned highlight, isolation and the hidden-selection notice; keeping both would ship two competing findings lists

decision: Review-incomplete findings became selectable evidence rows that open the engine's own reason
why: They rendered as inert list items, so a reviewer could see that something was undecided but never why — the one state the product refuses to let read as a pass

decision: Layout assertions settle CSS transitions before measuring geometry
why: Buttons carry transition-all, so heights read mid-animation right after setViewportSize; three "undersized control" failures were measurement artefacts, proven by a synthetic control with identical classes measuring 44px in the same parent

decision: An undecided requirement now states so in its own evidence panel instead of borrowing the not-applicable scope sentence
why: The review-incomplete fixture finding rendered 「対象外として判定されました」 — the exact confusion the product forbids; the panel now leads with the undecided statement plus the engine's own reasons

decision: Every browser scenario now serves a production build; the viewer scenario stopped using next dev
why: Dev-mode Tailwind served a stale utility sheet after component edits, so touch-target and layout assertions passed or failed on cache state rather than on the shipped CSS
